Most devoted painter: Edvard Weie, in 11 of 33 works here (5.6x the baseline of the museums those works come from; as photographed 4.4x; n=11).

First seen in our archive in 1190 (cma-140153, by Wu Bing); the third-earliest painting is 1275, and the latest 1950 (909 dated paintings, at least 2% of the canvas, as photographed). The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first. That is 722 years before the name's earliest record in our sources (1912): the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of the pigment or dye.
Shares canvases with Pois Green and Greyish hunter green more than chance (lift 7.8 and 7.6; n=78 and 112).
In printed English the word peaks in the 1880s and rose fastest in the 1840s (Google Books, all senses of the word, so a color name that is also an object or a place can mislead).
